title: Implement a VCF Installer 9.0 token-refreshing deployment client
prompt:
Implement the unfinished `vcf_installer` package in `src/vcf_installer` as a Python 3.11+ standard-library-only client for the VCF Installer 9.0 contract in `docs/contract.json`. Complete `VCFInstallerClient.create_token`, `refresh_access_token`, `deploy_sddc`, `get_sddc_task`, and `deploy_and_wait`, while preserving the public signatures in the starter code. Requests and responses are JSON: token creation sends only non-`None` credential fields using the contract's exact field names; deployment sends the supplied SDDC specification unchanged; an unset `skip_validations` omits `skipValidations` from the URL entirely; and refresh sends the refresh-token ID as a JSON string, not an object. Send `Accept: application/json` on every request, `Content-Type: application/json` when there is a body, and `Authorization: Bearer <access token>` only on deployment and status requests. Store the token pair returned by `createToken`. If an authenticated request receives HTTP 401, call `refreshAccessToken` with the stored refresh-token ID, store its JSON-string response as the new access token, and retry only the failed request so an accepted deployment is not submitted again. `deploy_and_wait` must submit once, poll the same installation ID through `getSddcTaskByID`, sleep by `poll_interval` between nonterminal results, and return the terminal SDDC task. Raise `InstallerAPIError` for other HTTP failures, retaining the HTTP status and parsed response body where possible.

Run `python3 -B verify.py` to check your work. The verifier, its loopback service, the contract documents, `pyproject.toml`, and `src/vcf_installer/__init__.py` are fixed inputs; do not modify them.
